claim: Basis used for every population comparison here: ONE year (2026) and ONE basis (1 July). States: the National Commission on Population Technical Group's official projection (Nov 2019), Table 11, 1 July 2026. Countries: UN DESA World Population Prospects 2024, medium variant, 1 July 2026. India's total on the NCP table is 14,26,907 thousand (1,426.9 million).

evidence.locator: Appendix 2, Table 11 (1 July), page with INDIA, J&K, Himachal; row 2026 (excerpt line 38)

method: method/states_pop_rank.py parses Table 11 (sources/ncp_table11_1july_excerpt.txt) into method/ncp_table11_parsed.json; the 37 states/UTs sum to 1,426,888 thousand against the printed India 1,426,907 (method/match_countries_output.txt, first lines).
notes: Not a count: the last count is Census 2011 and the next has a reference date of 1 March 2027 (verified in sibling W3-01-up, its C019; not re-cited here under the lite source cap). We use 1 July to match the UN's 1 July.

claim: Uttar Pradesh: 243,466 thousand (about 24.3 crore) on 1 July 2026 (NCP projection). If every Indian state were a country and India did not exist as one, UP would be the FIFTH most populous country in the world in 2026, behind China, the United States, Indonesia and Pakistan, and just ahead of Nigeria.

evidence.quote: 4 Pakistan 259,300k C 5 Uttar Pradesh 243,466k S 6 Nigeria 242,432k C

method: method/combined_world.py: all 37 NCP states/UTs plus the 236 WPP countries/areas other than India, sorted (273 entities).
notes: CONFLICT with W3-01-up, which ranks UP sixth because it keeps 'the rest of India' as a country. Both are right in their own frame; see conflicts.md K1. Sensitivity B (states scaled to the UN's higher India total): still fifth (251,949k). Not used as a spine claim: the sibling Short W3-01-up owns UP (it uses the 'rest of India kept' frame, sixth). Here the frame is India dissolved into states, so UP is fifth; never mix the frames on screen.

claim: Maharashtra versus Japan: Maharashtra 129,584 thousand against Japan 122,428 thousand in 2026 (+5.8%; +9.5% on the scaled basis). On 1 July 2011 Maharashtra (112,798 thousand, NCP) was 11.9% behind Japan (128,096 thousand, UN): the order flipped because Japan shrank and Maharashtra grew.
method: method/lite_pairs.py (A = NCP as printed; B = NCP x UN India/NCP India; 2011 = NCP 1 July 2011 vs WPP 1 July 2011).
notes: Projection-dependent: the 'ahead of Japan' result needs the NCP growth path. Japan's own population falls over the same period in WPP (128.1 to 122.4 million).

claim: Bihar versus Mexico: Bihar 132,850 thousand against Mexico 132,998 thousand in 2026 (-0.1%; +3.4% on the scaled basis): the same population. On our Natural Earth measure Mexico's land (1,962,242 sq km) is 20.7 times Bihar's (94,876 sq km).
method: method/lite_pairs.py; areas measured by us on Natural Earth 1:10m geometry (authalic sphere), same basis for state and country.
notes: Say 'about the same as Mexico' and 'about twenty times the land'. The 1 Nov run's Census/FAO areas (94,163 vs 1,960,647; 20.8x) agree (method/pairs_output.txt, kept for reference).

claim: Rajasthan versus Germany: 83,879 thousand against 83,644 thousand in 2026 (+0.3%; +3.8% on the scaled basis), and nearly the same land on our Natural Earth measure: 343,697 against 356,379 sq km (Germany 1.04 times).

evidence.quote: Rajasthan vs Germany | 2026 A 83,879k vs 83,644k +0.3% | B 86,802k +3.8%

notes: The only pair matching on both people and land (density 244 vs 235 per sq km). On 1 July 2011 Rajasthan (68,928k NCP) was 14.8% behind Germany (80,858k): the match is a 2026 projection.

claim: In 2026 UP is larger than 232 of the 236 countries and areas in the UN list (other than India), and 22 of India's 37 states and UTs have more people than the median country in the UN list (5.7 million).

evidence.quote: Countries/areas in WPP smaller than UP (2026 basis A): 232 of 236
states/UTs with 2026 pop above the median country: 22 of 37

notes: Includes small non-sovereign areas, so say 'than the typical country in the UN list', not 'than most nations'.

claim: The NCP projection has Bihar overtaking Maharashtra in 2023 (1 July): 127,368 thousand against 126,710 thousand; in 2026 132,850 against 129,584; in 2011 (1 July) Maharashtra was ahead, 112,798 against 104,771.
method: Year-by-year read from Table 11; method/pairs_output.txt tail lists the crossing.
notes: A projection, not a count; Census 2027 will show whether it happened.

claim: Crowding, 2026 projection over our Natural Earth areas: Bihar about 1,400 people per sq km against Mexico's 68; Kerala about 960 against Malaysia's 110; West Bengal about 1,160 against Vietnam's 310.
method: method/lite_pairs.py: NCP (state) or WPP (country) 1 July 2026 population over Natural Earth area, one area basis for both.
notes: Say 'about'. Natural Earth geometry is generalised (within about 1.5% of Census/FAO areas).

claim: The UN's own India estimate for 2026 (1,476.6 million) is 3.5% higher than the Indian projection (1,426.9 million). So 'state in the UN table' needs a stated basis: as printed by India's own projection, or scaled to the UN's total. All rankings in the pairs hold or are 'level' on both.
notes: The UN estimate is its own harmonised series, not India's count. Use the Indian projection for states because the pitch is about Indian states and the NCP is the official one [C001].

claim: The five comparison countries are sovereign states in the UN's list (Nigeria, Japan, Mexico, Germany, United Kingdom) and the WPP file lists them under LocTypeName 'Country/Area'; the file also lists non-sovereign areas (for example Macao, Kosovo), which is why the median in C009 is for 'countries and areas'.
notes: Kosovo's status is disputed internationally: do not use it or Macao in the Short.
